title: Enhanced Performance of Brain Tumor Classification via Tumor Region Augmentation and Partition
major_contribution: Original benchmark on the 3064 T1-CE MRI dataset using tumor region augmentation and patient-level splitting
limitations: Handcrafted features rather than modern end-to-end deep learning
our_takeaway: Defines the canonical benchmark dataset and establishes the gold standard for patient-level evaluation.

title: Automated Brain Tumor Detection From Magnetic Resonance Images Using Fine-Tuned EfficientNet-B4 Convolutional Neural Network
major_contribution: Applied fine-tuned EfficientNet-B4 to multi-class brain tumor detection with Grad-CAM visualization
limitations: Did not enforce patient-level grouping across slices causing potential slice leakage; no confidence calibration
our_takeaway: Demonstrates strong representation power of EfficientNet-B4 on brain MRI but highlights need for patient-level partitioning.

title: Enhancing EfficientNetv2 with Global and Efficient Channel Attention Mechanisms for Accurate MRI-Based Brain Tumor Classification
major_contribution: Integrated Global Attention Mechanism (GAM) and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) into EfficientNetV2
limitations: Random slice-level K-Fold instead of patient-disjoint folds; no uncertainty estimation
our_takeaway: Attention mechanisms boost feature saliency; however strict patient-disjoint splits are essential to confirm generalization.

title: Deep-EFNet: An Optimized EfficientNetB0 Architecture With Dual Regularization for Scalable Multi-Class Brain Tumor Classification in MRI
major_contribution: Lightweight EfficientNetB0 with custom regularization blocks achieving low computational complexity
limitations: Random slice partitioning without patient ID tracking; no test-time calibration or robustness testing
our_takeaway: Proves that smaller EfficientNet variants (B0) provide competitive accuracy at a fraction of compute cost.

title: T3SSLNet: Triple-Method Self-Supervised Learning for Enhanced Brain Tumor Classification in MRI
major_contribution: Triple self-supervised pre-training to learn robust representations from unlabeled MRI scans
limitations: High training complexity with contrastive pairs; no confidence calibration or robustness quantification
our_takeaway: Self-supervised features stabilize downstream representations; ResNet50 remains a formidable baseline.

title: Rethinking model of EfficientNet-B9 for Brain Tumor Classification: A High-Precision Deep Learning Approach
major_contribution: Proposed scaled deep architecture beyond standard compound coefficients for MRI classification
limitations: Overparameterized without patient-level validation; risk of severe overfitting to scanner artifacts
our_takeaway: Heavier compound scales yield diminishing returns and escalate deployment latency on clinical edge devices.

title: Effect of data leakage in brain MRI classification using deep learning
major_contribution: Rigorously proved that slice-level random splitting produces up to 10-15% artificial accuracy inflation due to patient identity leakage
limitations: Did not explore EfficientNet compound scaling or calibration
our_takeaway: Foundational justification for our patient-level StratifiedGroupKFold design.

title: Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM): 2024 Update
major_contribution: Formal 2024 reporting standard encompassing dataset partitioning
column29: Guideline paper without specific modeling code
column30: Forms the methodological compliance backbone for our entire study.
